label: EU(7)-PIM: pioglitazone
title: Pioglitazone in an older person
statement: Pioglitazone | In lists: 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Age-related risks include bladder cancer, fractures and heart failure. Use for more than one year has been associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer. May increase the incidence of fractures of the upper arms, hands and feet in female diabetics (compared to other oral antidiabetic agents). Can cause fluid retention in older adults, which may exacerbate or precipitate heart failure | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: Diet; metformin (<2 x 850 mg/d); insulin; gliclazide may be safer than the other short-acting sulphonilureas. E

plain_summary: Pioglitazone can cause fluid retention that may bring on or worsen heart failure in older people, and is linked to broken bones in women and, after more than a year of use, to bladder cancer.

medicine_groups.name: Pioglitazone
medicine_groups.note: Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a Group A medicine (pioglitazone) is supplied, at any dose, to a patient aged 65 years or over. If age is missing and the other requirements are met, report only a possible finding and ask for the patient's age. One supply is enough. A patient aged under 65 years is not a finding.
cannot_be_seen: Use any recorded heart failure, leg swelling, fracture, osteoporosis, current or past bladder cancer, blood glucose or HbA1c result. If a detail is missing, dispensing alone cannot establish it. Earlier pioglitazone exposure may extend beyond the period shown.
ask_the_gp: Could you review whether pioglitazone still suits the patient's age, considering the risk of new or worsening heart failure, fracture risk and any bladder problems?
